title: Economic Growth
tagline: The facts of growth, the Solow model, technology and growth accounting, convergence, optimal saving in the Ramsey model, overlapping generations, ideas and endogenous growth, and institutions
summary: Small differences in growth rates compound into vast differences in living standards. This course asks why some countries are rich and others poor, and why growth happens at all: the stylised facts, capital accumulation in the Solow model and growth accounting, convergence, optimal saving in the Ramsey–Cass–Koopmans and overlapping-generations models, the economics of ideas and endogenous growth, and the deeper roles of institutions and geography.

chapters.title: The facts of economic growth
chapters.summary: Growth over two centuries, Kaldor’s stylised facts, the world distribution of income and the power of compounding.

chapters.title: The Solow model
chapters.summary: Capital accumulation with diminishing returns, the steady state, the golden rule and transitional dynamics.

chapters.title: Technological progress and growth accounting
chapters.summary: Labour-augmenting technology, balanced growth, and the decomposition of growth into capital, labour and total factor productivity.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Absolute and conditional convergence, human capital in the augmented Solow model, and the evidence across countries.

chapters.title: Optimal saving: the Ramsey–Cass–Koopmans model
chapters.summary: Households that optimise over time, the Euler equation, the saddle path and the efficiency of the competitive equilibrium.

chapters.title: Overlapping generations
chapters.summary: The Diamond model, dynamic inefficiency, and the effects of pay-as-you-go pensions and public debt.

chapters.title: Ideas and endogenous growth
chapters.summary: The non-rivalry of ideas, the AK and Romer models, research and development, and scale effects.

chapters.title: Institutions, geography and the deep causes of growth
chapters.summary: Property rights, colonial origins, geography and culture, and the empirical debate over the fundamental causes of prosperity.
